messages.author: 6eec351ad1d5a711
messages.subject: Indexing issue
parts:
Hi,
Im trying to transfer some code over from a JAGS model but having some issues with indexing within the model code. The original code was this:

 # define cell probabilities of the multistate m-array
 #  (Matrix U: product of probabilities of state-transition and non-encounter,
 #  which is needed because there is no 'product' function for matrix
 #  multiplication in JAGS):
  for(t in 1:(occ-2)){
    U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(t-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- ones
    for(j in (t+1):(occ-1)){
      U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(j-1)*ns+(1:ns)] <- U[(t-1)*ns+(1:ns),(j-2)*ns+(1:ns)] %*% Psi[,j-1,] %*% dq[,j-1,]
    } #j
  } #t

where ones = diag(ns) and now given in constants.

But this code gives the error:
Defining model Error : Error processing model: something is wrong with the index oPt_minus_1_cP_times_7 + (1:7). Indexing in model code requires this syntax: '(start expression):(end expression)'. Error: Error occurred defining U[oPt_minus_1_cP_times_7 + (1:7), oPt_minus_1_cP_times_7 + (1:7)]

I can add an addition loop for 1:ns which gets round the issue but Im wondering if there is a quicker way/what the issue is?

Any suggestions very gratefully received!  
Cheers
Dave

messages.author: 6eec351ad1d5a711
messages.subject: Re: Indexing issue
parts:
OK, Thanks to Wei Zhang for the solution which I thought I had tried but I must have typed something wrong when trying!

Anyway - solution 1 + (t-1)*ns) : (ns + (t-1)*ns) in case anyone has a similar issue.


Thanks very much!
Dave

messages.author: 7878556d408ec9ec
messages.subject: Re: Indexing issue
parts:
Hi Dave,

You might need to change your index (t-1)*ns+(1:ns) to (1 + (t-1)*ns) : (ns + (t-1)*ns); and similarly for (j-1)*ns+(1:ns). Nimble requires (start expression):(end expression) style index range. 

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: Indexing issue with constants
parts:
I also have an indexing issue that I can't seem to debug. below is a reproducible code with a tiny data set that triggers the error.  
constants<-list(N = c(7, 8, 5),
           g=rep(1,20),
           starts = c(1, 8, 16), # where in the vector g to start observing values
           ends =  c(7, 15, 20), # where in the vector g to stop observing values
           nsites = 3
)
str(constants)

 ## Define model in BUGS language as nimbleCode object
  N_DO_negbin_code <- nimble::nimbleCode({
    mu ~ dunif(0,100)
    r ~ dunif(0,100)
    alpha ~ dunif(0,100)
    p<-r/(r+mu)
   
    for(i in 1:nsites){
      N[i] ~ dnbinom(prob=p,size=r)
      start <- starts[i]
      end <- ends[i]
      g[start:end] ~ dCRP(conc=alpha, size=N[i]) # be careful, N=0 returns 1!
    }
  })
 
  DO_inits <- function(){list(
    mu=10,
    r=1,
    alpha=0.5
    )
  }
  initsList <- DO_inits()
  # Define parameters to save and MCMC settings
  params <- c("mu","r","p")
 
  # Call NIMBLE, plot posterior distributions
  DO_model<-nimble::nimbleModel(code = N_DO_negbin_code,
                                constants = constants, inits = initsList)

mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(model = DO_model, nchains = 1, inits = initsFunction,
                       samples = FALSE, summary = TRUE)

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Indexing issue with constants
parts:
Hi Dave,

Let me comment on a couple things related to indexing and dCRP that I think are causing problems here. 

1.) One can use variables in an index sequence, such as `g[start:end]`, but if doing so, `start` and `end` must be fixed constants.

So you would want:

```
g[starts[i]:ends[i]] ~ dCRP(alpha, size=lens[i])
```

with `starts` and `ends` being vectors specified via `constants`. Your code tries to use `g[start:end]` as if the for loop was code being interpreted and `start` and `end` were being repeatedly re-defined, but the modeling language is for declaring the nodes in the model structure, and one can repeated redefine `start` and `end`.

`lens` should also be a vector in `constants` giving the length of `g[starts[i]:ends[i]]`. See next point.

2.) In the dCRP specification, the `size` can't be random. It must be the length of `g[starts[i]:ends[i]]`.   (Ideally we wouldn't even make users provide `size` and we would just infer what it is from the left-hand side of the declaration but that is hard for us to do for reasons not worth going into.)

-Chris

I'll also say that  it may be the case that we can improve some error messages... I will give that some thought.
